doc.brief: An interface that adds support for selection to list models.
doc.md:
An interface that adds support for selection to list models.

This support is then used by widgets using list models to add the ability
to select and unselect various items.

GTK provides default implementations of the most common selection modes such
as [`SingleSelection`](xref:gtk:Gtk.SingleSelection), so you will only need to implement this
interface if you want detailed control about how selections should be handled.

A `GtkSelectionModel` supports a single boolean per item indicating if an item is
selected or not. This can be queried via [`SelectionModel.is_selected()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.SelectionModel#method:is_selected).
When the selected state of one or more items changes, the model will emit the
[`SelectionModel::selection-changed`](xref:gtk:Gtk.SelectionModel#event:selection-changed) signal by calling the
[`SelectionModel.selection_changed()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.SelectionModel#method:selection_changed) function. The positions given
in that signal may have their selection state changed, though that is not a
requirement. If new items added to the model via the
[`ListModel::items-changed`](xref:gtk:Gio.ListModel#event:items-changed) signal are selected or not is up to the
implementation.

Note that items added via [`ListModel::items-changed`](xref:gtk:Gio.ListModel#event:items-changed) may already
be selected and no [`SelectionModel::selection-changed`](xref:gtk:Gtk.SelectionModel#event:selection-changed) will be
emitted for them. So to track which items are selected, it is necessary to
listen to both signals.

Additionally, the interface can expose functionality to select and unselect
items. If these functions are implemented, GTK's list widgets will allow users
to select and unselect items. However, `GtkSelectionModel`s are free to only
implement them partially or not at all. In that case the widgets will not
support the unimplemented operations.

When selecting or unselecting is supported by a model, the return values of
the selection functions do *not* indicate if selection or unselection happened.
They are only meant to indicate complete failure, like when this mode of
selecting is not supported by the model.

Selections may happen asynchronously, so the only reliable way to find out
when an item was selected is to listen to the signals that indicate selection.

get_selection.brief: Gets the set containing all currently selected items in the model.
get_selection.md:
Gets the set containing all currently selected items in the model.

This function may be slow, so if you are only interested in single item,
consider using [`SelectionModel.is_selected()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.SelectionModel#method:is_selected) or if you are only
interested in a few, consider [`SelectionModel.get_selection_in_range()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.SelectionModel#method:get_selection_in_range).

get_selection_in_range.brief: Gets the set of selected items in a range.
get_selection_in_range.md:
Gets the set of selected items in a range.

This function is an optimization for
[`SelectionModel.get_selection()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.SelectionModel#method:get_selection) when you are only
interested in part of the model's selected state. A common use
case is in response to the [`SelectionModel::selection-changed`](xref:gtk:Gtk.SelectionModel#event:selection-changed)
signal.

is_selected.brief: Checks if the given item is selected.
is_selected.md: Checks if the given item is selected.

select_all.brief: Requests to select all items in the model.
select_all.md: Requests to select all items in the model.

select_item.brief: Requests to select an item in the model.
select_item.md: Requests to select an item in the model.

select_range.brief: Requests to select a range of items in the model.
select_range.md: Requests to select a range of items in the model.

selection_changed.md:
Helper function for implementations of `GtkSelectionModel`.

Call this when the selection changes to emit the
[`SelectionModel::selection-changed`](xref:gtk:Gtk.SelectionModel#event:selection-changed) signal.

unselect_all.brief: Requests to unselect all items in the model.
unselect_all.md: Requests to unselect all items in the model.

unselect_item.brief: Requests to unselect an item in the model.
unselect_item.md: Requests to unselect an item in the model.

unselect_range.brief: Requests to unselect a range of items in the model.
unselect_range.md: Requests to unselect a range of items in the model.

selection-changed.brief: Emitted when the selection state of some of the items in `model` changes.
selection-changed.md:
Emitted when the selection state of some of the items in `model` changes.

Note that this signal does not specify the new selection state of the
items, they need to be queried manually. It is also not necessary for
a model to change the selection state of any of the items in the selection
model, though it would be rather useless to emit such a signal.
